plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Since I don't pay my own bid (I pay the second-highest bid if I win), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. With my value at $49 (the maximum possible), bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win whenever profitable while paying only the second-highest bid.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) where the highest bidder wins but pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I underbid, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. If I overbid, I risk winning and paying more than my value. With a private value of $44, I should bid exactly $44 to ensure optimal outcomes.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing auctions you could have profitably won. Since my value is $22, I should bid exactly $22 to maximize expected profit.
